answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake in a shared trust kernel before trading. New identities start with tiny quotas, and only sustained, verifiable work raises their limit, so creating thousands of fakes multiplies locked capital, not influence. Like a river crossed only at guarded bridges, traffic passes audited checkpoints where past behavior is checked. A saffron merchant would trust a counterparty only after its kernel record shows repeated honest deliveries, making mass fakery expensive, slow, and easy to slash.
